value.rationale: Removing a single sparse word from the complete de Bruijn factor library is a natural constrained circular coverage problem. The theorem distinguishes impossibility, generic linear-overhead repair and a sharp parity-centered half-overhead, and determines precisely which permitted factors must be duplicated in any optimum. This is a complete infinite-family structural classification, not an arbitrary finite slice or restatement of the Euler theorem; general algorithms do not explicitly provide these closed-form consequences.
